To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the three stage process of lithium recovery from geothermal brine is feasible and can be simulated using the existing models; 2) the deterioration of the performance of the membranes used for membrane distillation is the main reason of the increase in the number of membrane modules required to be replaced; and 3) the energy efficiency of the process is low, and the increase of the membrane distillations efficiency and the energy efficiency of crystallizer are required.
the integrated system for lithium recovery from brine is feasible, but the energy consumption is high and needs improvement.

the three stage process of lithium recovery from brine can be simulated in Simulik/MATLAB and that the membrane distillation can be used for the concentration of lithium presence in brine from 0.1 g/kg up to 2-3 g/kg with the energy consumption of 0.5-0.6 kW/h.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the process of lithium recovery from geothermal brine and the results are important for the development of a sustainable lithium supply chain.
the development of the process for the recovery of lithium from geothermal waters and its implementation.
the development of the process simulation and the design of the integrated system for lithium recovery from geothermal waters.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the process simulation of the integrated membrane distillation crystallization membrane extraction system for lithium recovery from geothermal waters was carried out and the process parameters and their impact on the performance of the integrated system were identified and analyzed.
the integrated system of membrane distillation, crystallization and membrane extraction can be used as a promising alternative to the existing lithium recovery technologies.

the process of recovery of lithium ions from the geothermal brine by the proposed system can be considered as a promising alternative to the current methods of lithium recovery from the geothermal waters.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the simulation of the integrated system consisting of the membrane distillations unit, the crystallizer and the membrane extraction unit for the recovery of lithium ions from geothermal brine was successfully performed.
the process of lithium recovery from geothermal water by the integrated system consisting of the membrane distillations and crystallizer followed by the membrane lithium extraction is feasible.

the simulation of the three stage process of lithium recovery from geothermal brine including the brine pre-treatment by precipitation Ca2+ and Mg2+ cations and further concentration of the lithium presence in the saline solution by evaporation and precipitation of sodium chloride followed by membrane extraction of lithium from the solution with the membrane module of 1.5 m2 and the mass flow rate of the saline solution in the crystallizer of 6.5 g/min was performed.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the lithium recovery process from geothermal waters is possible but requires a lot of efforts to make it cost effective and energy efficient.
the integrated system of membrane distillation, crystallizer and membrane extraction can be used for the lithium recovery from geothermal brine.
the process of lithium recovery from the lithium-rich geothermal brine can be successfully simulated using the available data and models.
